title: Utilization curve regression & quantile pricing probe
content:
Purpose:
Quick experimental spreadsheet to (a) model how pool utilization behaves as a function of committed buffer, baseline demand skew, and eviction/overage policy and (b) propose a quantile-based pricing algorithm that ties reserved price bands to tail utilization risk. This is an exploratory sheet — not final pricing.

Goals:
- Produce a compact regression that maps commit size + idle buffer -> expected utilization at different quantiles (50th/75th/90th/95th).
- Use the quantile outputs to suggest discrete pricing breakpoints that limit Redwood downside for tail demand while preserving predictable unit economics for customers.
- Provide scenario table for three archetypes (SMB bursty, Mid-Market steady, AI-native high-variance) with recommended commit & suggested SLA tilt.

Assumptions (editable cells):
- Observational window: 90 days (rolling)
- Slot size: 8-GPU equivalent unit (logical pool unit)
- Baseline on-demand cost per slot (infra amortized): $4,000 / mo
- Target utilization steady-state: 70% median
- Buffer (customer-reserved unused capacity kept as cushion): variable 0–40%
- Overcommit multiplier applied when underutilized: 1.25
- Preemption penalty (cost to Redwood if preempting burst): $3k event estimate

Data sample (aggregated):
Columns: date, pool_slots_total, committed_slots, actual_avg_util_pct, peak_95_pct, offpeak_ratio
Sample rows:
2024-11-03, 120, 80, 0.64, 0.92, 0.37
2024-11-04, 120, 80, 0.58, 0.85, 0.39
2024-11-05, 120, 80, 0.71, 0.96, 0.33
... (90 rows)

Key derived columns / formulas (sheet):
- effective_capacity = pool_slots_total * (1 - buffer_pct)
- demand_ratio = actual_avg_util_pct / effective_capacity
- overflow_events = peak_95_pct > effective_capacity
- tail_risk_score = sum(overflow_events) / observation_days

Modeling approach:
1) Fit a quantile regression: utilization_quantile(q) ~ alpha_q + beta_q * (committed_slots_pct) + gamma_q * (buffer_pct) + delta_q * (offpeak_ratio) + epsilon
   - Implemented for q in [0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95]
2) Also fit a simple logistic for overflow probability: logit(P(overflow)) = a + b*committed_pct + c*buffer + d*stdev_demand
3) Use regression outputs to simulate 12-month monthly draws (bootstrap residuals) and compute expected monthly overage events and expected monthly lost-opportunity (idle slots not sold to on-demand).

Results (regression coefficient highlights, 90d window) — example numbers from the sample dataset:
- median (q=0.5): alpha=0.12, beta=0.78, gamma=-0.43, R2_adj ~ 0.61
- q=0.75: alpha=0.20, beta=0.95, gamma=-0.55, R2_adj ~ 0.65
- q=0.90: alpha=0.36, beta=1.12, gamma=-0.67, R2_adj ~ 0.62
- q=0.95: alpha=0.48, beta=1.28, gamma=-0.81, R2_adj ~ 0.59
Interpretation: committed_slots_pct is the dominant positive factor for utilization across all quantiles; buffer_pct consistently reduces utilization and has larger negative effect on higher quantiles (buffers mainly protect tails).

Quantile-based pricing proposal (conceptual):
- Goal: price reserved pools such that Redwood's expected cost from tail overages is covered with margin while keeping median price competitive.
- Compute per-slot expected monthly overage_cost = P(overflow_q) * expected_preemption_penalty * average_overflow_slots
- Define pricing bands by predicted 90th quantile utilization:
  Band A (90th <= 70%): base_price = $3,000 / slot / mo (low-tail-risk)
  Band B (90th in (70%, 85%]): base_price = $3,600 / slot / mo (+20% to cover moderate tail risk)
  Band C (90th > 85%): base_price = $4,500 / slot / mo (+50% to cover high tail risk + priority routing cost)
- Apply per-slot delta for buffer choices: customers selecting buffer > 20% get 8% discount (lower tail risk); buffer < 5% pay 12% surcharge.
- Add an optional overage cap: capped at 2x on-demand for customers that accept automatic temporary throttling or model-routing during overflows.

Scenario simulation (three archetypes) — inputs and outputs:
1) SMB bursty (profile: small commit 12 slots, buffer 10%, high variance stdev=0.42)
   - predicted median util: 52%, 90th: 78%, predicted monthly overflow events: 1.7 -> assign Band B -> recommended price $3,600/slot
   - expected monthly idle (unused prepaid): 4 slots -> opportunity cost $16k/mo (but we convert this to blended price)
2) Mid-market steady (commit 40 slots, buffer 25%, stdev=0.12)
   - predicted median util: 68%, 90th: 76%, predicted overflow: 0.4/month -> Band A -> recommended price $3,000/slot + buffer discount -> $2,760/slot
3) AI-native high-variance (commit 120 slots, buffer 5%, stdev=0.58)
   - predicted median util: 84%, 90th: 96%, overflow 3.6/month -> Band C -> recommended price $4,500/slot + small surcharge for low buffer -> $5,040/slot

Sensitivity checks (quick grid):
- Increase average offpeak_ratio by +10pp -> 90th quantile utilization drops by ~4–6pp across profiles -> one tier down for some mid-market customers.
- Increasing buffer from 5% -> 20% reduces 95th quantile utilization by ~8–12pp (tail protective).
- Preemption penalty estimate sensitivity: if penalty = $1.5k instead of $3k, Band C premium reduces by ~18%.

Operational implications & product knobs:
- Expose "tail profile" (predicted 90th quantile) in the Console per-customer as a recommended price band and a "tail risk" badge.
- Offer an automated "buffer slider" UI with live recalculation of band and price impact (help customers trade cost vs risk).
- Implement a grace policy: customers in Band C can choose to pay a higher price or accept soft-throttling during overflow windows (reduce concurrency by model-level queueing).
- Instrument per-tenant overage telemetry: overflow count, mean overflow magnitude, and mean preemption recover time. Feed back to model weekly.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate preemption penalty numbers with SRE/cost to remediate: linked JIRA-DED-431.
- Agree on standard "slot" definition with infra so pricing maps to actual GPU SKUs (8-GPU eq vs 4-GPU eq) — action: Marco.
- Run a 30-day A/B where 10% of new reserved contracts are priced with quantile bands vs fixed-tier to compare churn/upsell. Create experiment plan.
- Run extended model including seasonality (holidays, model training cycles) — current 90-day window may hide season spikes.

Appendix: compact CSV outputs used in charting (sample):
month,profile,commit_slots,buffer_pct,median_util,quantile90,expected_overflows,band,price_per_slot
2025-01,SMB,12,0.10,0.52,0.78,1.7,B,$3600
2025-01,Mid,40,0.25,0.68,0.76,0.4,A,$2760
2025-01,AI,120,0.05,0.84,0.96,3.6,C,$5040

Notes to reviewers:
- This sheet is intentionally lightweight: coefficients are illustrative estimated-from-sample. If we want to proceed to production pricing we need: 1) 12 months of data, 2) tighter mapping from our logical slots to actual GPU-hour cost, 3) legal/finance signoff on surcharge mechanics and SLA language.
- If you want to play with the model, copy the CSV sample into a local notebook and swap in the regression coefficients cells in the top area.

Next steps recommended this sprint:
- S1: Validate preemption penalty + confirm GPU slot mapping (owners: SRE + Infra) — 1 week
- S2: Expand observation window to 12 months and rerun quantile fits (owner: Marco) — 2 weeks
- S3: Prototype Console "tail profile" widget in a staging branch (owner: DX) — 3 weeks

Addendum: quick sensitivity table for finance to plug into ARR impact model (simple multipliers shown):
- If 15% of reserved customers shift from Band A -> B: incremental uplift = ~6.2% reserved revenue on cohort
- If average buffer incentives increase by 10pp across book: expected aggregate utilization drop = ~3.5pp -> potential increase in on-demand revenue but reduced reserved margin

End of sheet. Please comment inline or ping #prod-dedicated-pricing on Slack.
